title: Cameron's years with Dannie Richmond's group after Mingus
summary: Brown notes Cameron played with George Adams, Don Pullen and Dannie Richmond for eight and a half years after Mingus's death, and Cameron wrote a lullaby for them.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I want to add a footnote at this point to let the audience know that Cameron Brown played with George Adams, Don Pullen and Dannie Richmond in the group following Mingus‟s death in ‟79. Brown, C.: Right.
So Cameron has a very, a very close and, uh, I would say a very intimate relationship, a musically intimate relationship with Dannie Richmond so…
And I just wanted to make sure… Brown, C.: Eight and a half years.
Yeah. Brown, C.: I mean, that band was working probably almost half the time.
Right. Brown, C.: Which is a lot for a band to work. I mean, in and out, you know, but…
Mm-hmm. Brown, C.: …it was three European tours, three or four weeks at the Vanguard for Japan. A few gigs in the States. Little, little California things every now and then.
Right, right. But just to contextualize the, uh, dedication to Dannie Richmond. Brown, C.: Yeah, yeah.
Oh, yeah. Brown, C.: Oh, yeah. Well….
Oh, he loved those cats, Cameron. Brown, C.: [inaudible].

Those are his soulmates. [laughs] Brown, C.: Yeah. I wrote a lullaby dedicated to all three of them when George passed away. And uh, wrote lyrics to it, and um, and then I‟m on my second… from this project in Belgium, second, the second CD volume II, we used Sheila‟s Morning Song as an introduction, and then she sang this ballad that I wrote for them so beautifully on that.
